- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift (increasing trend) while true outcomes often exhibit sharp drops or volatility, suggesting model fails to capture short-term volatility or mean reversion.
- After a price spike, model continues to rise slightly beyond true outcome, indicating overshoot bias.
- Model underestimates true outcomes in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting lag or failure to respond to recent downward trends.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in history, leading to persistent overestimation even when recent data shows downward pressure.
- Forecasts are smoother than true outcomes, indicating model lacks sensitivity to sharp reversals or sudden drops.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices — overconfidence in continuation of trend.
- Correction should involve reducing forecast slope after spikes and incorporating recent low values more heavily in weighting.
